claims.statement: DORA requires financial entities to maintain a register of information covering contractual arrangements for ICT services supplied by third parties and permits supervisors to request the full register or parts of it.
The implementing regulation defines standard templates and relational keys including contract reference, entity/provider identifiers, function identifier and ICT service type.

In the ESA dry run involving almost 1000 financial entities, only 6.5% of registers passed every data-quality check and half of the remainder failed fewer than five of 116 checks, showing both real errors and a tractable validation surface.

contrary_evidence: Half of dry-run registers that did not fully pass still failed fewer than five checks, so many entities may need only a spreadsheet cleanup rather than ongoing software.
EBA publishes templates, FAQs and validation resources for free.
GRC suites, consulting firms and legal advisers already serve DORA programmes.

economics.acquisition_route: Sell a fixed 6000-12000 PLN health check to five entities through one compliance boutique, measure errors and update labour, then convert the adviser to a portfolio licence.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Four hundred entity licences averaging 20000 PLN annually would produce 8m PLN recurring revenue. At a mature 45% owner-cash margin, 3.6m PLN per year could generate over 10m PLN cumulative distributions across four mature years without an exit.
economics.founder_time: Build only extraction, reconciliation and official-check coverage at 3-5 hours/day, with licensed advisers owning legal interpretation; leave employment only after repeat adviser-led renewals, contribution economics and runway meet the stated gates.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Rule execution and export are software-heavy, but contract setup and regulatory updates require expert operations; target 65-80% gross margin after partner support.
economics.payback: Target customer payback within one reporting or material contract-update cycle versus adviser and staff time; enforcement risk alone should not be used as the ROI claim.
economics.pricing: Assumption to test: 8000-30000 PLN annual licence per regulated entity by contract volume plus 5000-20000 PLN onboarding; adviser portfolio pricing preserves at least 60% of list revenue.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Registers must be maintained as contracts and providers change and can be requested by supervisors; annual reporting and version history support renewal, though workload may be episodic.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A contract-clause ontology, vendor identity graph and labelled validation-resolution corpus improve extraction and catch cross-template inconsistencies while preserving tenant confidentiality.
fingerprint.customer: Small Polish and EU payment institutions, insurers, investment firms and other DORA-covered entities, plus compliance boutiques maintaining registers for multiple clients.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Compliance boutiques, DORA legal advisers and GRC resellers deliver the workspace to their client portfolios; a fixed-price register health check is the initial product.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Private-cloud or local workspace that extracts contract clauses and identifiers into the official relational templates, resolves LEI/EUID/vendor links, records human approvals, runs current technical/business checks and exports a submission package; annual licence plus onboarding.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The compliance or ICT-risk owner pays per legal entity and vendor-contract count when the register is refreshed and validated; existing spend is staff, legal review, GRC tooling and reporting consultancy.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: An ICT contract is signed, renewed, subcontracted or reclassified as supporting a critical function, or a regulator requests the current register in prescribed templates.

founder_fit: Relational data validation, extraction and entity resolution strongly fit a data scientist.
One adviser can bring many regulated clients, reducing meeting-heavy direct sales.
The scope is a narrow deterministic register rather than open-ended security consulting.
A read-only health-check service can validate demand within the available capital and alongside employment.
risks: Missing a subcontractor, critical function or identifier could produce a materially incomplete register.
ICT contracts expose security architecture, vendors and sensitive commercial terms.
Regulatory interpretation can drift beyond a software founder's competence and must remain adviser-owned.
Large GRC vendors can bundle the register at low incremental price.

structure.commercial_archetype: Regulatory data-quality workspace sold annually per legal entity
structure.control_point: The approved source-of-truth that links each ICT contract, service, provider, function and reporting identifier
structure.critical_dependency: Exact maintenance of ESA templates and checks plus secure access to confidential ICT contracts and corporate hierarchy data

thesis: Offer smaller EU-regulated financial firms and their compliance advisers a contract-to-register workspace that extracts ICT service facts, reconciles entity/vendor/function keys and runs official DORA register data-quality checks before reporting. Financial entities already pay compliance staff and consultants to maintain the mandatory register; the narrow wedge is a version-controlled source of truth and preflight, not broad cybersecurity consulting.
title: DORA ICT-Contract Register Data-Quality Validator
uncertainties: The number of small Polish covered entities without an adequate GRC solution is unknown.
Official 2026 reporting cadence and national supervisory submission practices need confirmation per entity type.
Contract extraction accuracy and adviser liability allocation require controlled tests.
Pricing, margins, account count and wealth projections are unsourced assumptions.
